meta.source: Luminari CA Registry v1.0 — Northwest Hope Foundation
meta.disclaimer: General guidance — not legal advice. Deadlines are statutory and must be respected. Californians facing legal deadlines should contact LAFLA (800-399-4529) or local legal aid immediately.

workflow_overrides.situation: Landlord fails to make repairs, shuts off utilities, or retaliates against tenant

steps.description: Photograph all violations with timestamps. Keep all landlord communications in writing. Note health impacts, dates discovered, temperatures if heat issue.
steps.documents_needed: Photos, texts/emails, notes with dates — keep copies off-site
steps.deadline: Immediately — creates evidence base

steps.description: Send written notice (certified mail + keep copy) citing Civil Code §1941. Give reasonable time to repair — 30 days for non-urgent, less for urgent habitability.
steps.agency_contact: Landlord via certified mail + text/email — document delivery
steps.deadline: Required step before most legal remedies

steps.description: File complaint with local code enforcement or housing inspection. LA City: 213-808-8808 (LAHD). SF: 415-558-6220. Other cities: call 211 for local building dept.
steps.deadline: Within days — urgent health/safety prioritized

steps.description: Contact local legal aid. LA: LAFLA (800-399-4529) or Bet Tzedek (323-939-0506). Bay Area: Bay Area Legal Aid (415-982-1300). Under CC §1942: rent withholding or repair-and-deduct after written notice.
steps.agency_contact: LA: LAFLA 800-399-4529; Bay Area: BALA 415-982-1300; Statewide: lawhelpca.org
steps.deadline: If landlord does not repair after notice + reasonable time

steps.description: If landlord retaliates (raises rent, serves eviction notice) within 180 days of complaint, retaliation is presumed illegal under Civil Code §1942.5. Document timeline carefully.
steps.agency_contact: Legal aid + LAHD or local housing authority
steps.deadline: Retaliation presumed unlawful within 180 days of protected activity — CC §1942.5

steps.description: File complaint with CA Attorney General (800-952-5225). If rent control jurisdiction (LA, SF, Oakland), file with local rent board. HUD Fair Housing if discrimination involved.
steps.deadline: If code enforcement or local agency does not respond within 30 days

workflow_overrides.situation: Employer fails to pay wages, overtime, minimum wage, final paycheck, or illegally deducts wages
workflow_overrides.ca_statute: CA Labor Code §200–244 (wages); §510 (overtime); §1194 (minimum wage private right of action)

steps.description: Gather pay stubs, time records, offer letter, schedules. Calculate all unpaid amounts: regular wages, overtime (1.5x after 8 hrs/day or 40 hrs/wk in CA), missed meal/rest break premiums, final paycheck delays.
steps.documents_needed: Pay stubs, time records, offer letter, schedule
steps.deadline: CA SOL: 3 years for unpaid wages (LC §338); 4 years for UCL claim — start immediately

steps.description: Send written demand to employer. Keep copy. Final paycheck: CA requires same-day for termination, within 72 hours for resignation — every day late triggers 1 day waiting time penalty.
steps.documents_needed: Written demand letter with specific amounts
steps.deadline: Final pay waiting time penalty accrues daily — document demand immediately

steps.description: File wage claim with CA Division of Labor Standards Enforcement (DLSE) / Labor Commissioner. Free. Claims conference usually within 30 days. DLSE can award wages + penalties + attorney's fees.
steps.agency_contact: DLSE: 844-522-6734 / dir.ca.gov/dlse — file online or at local office
steps.deadline: 3-year SOL for wages; 1-year for waiting time penalty — file promptly

steps.description: If federal FLSA applies, also file with Wage and Hour Division (WHD). CA overtime law is more generous than federal — pursue both when applicable.
steps.deadline: FLSA: 2-year SOL (3 if willful) — file simultaneously with DLSE

steps.description: For claims up to $12,500, may file in Small Claims Court without attorney. DLSE process is usually preferable because DLSE has enforcement power.
steps.deadline: Alternative to DLSE — simpler but limited remedies

steps.description: If retaliated against for filing, contact legal aid. CA Labor Code §1102.5 (whistleblower), §98.6 (wage claim retaliation) — strong CA protections. CRLA for farmworkers (415-777-2752).
steps.deadline: File retaliation complaint within 6 months of retaliatory act

workflow_overrides.situation: CalFresh, Medi-Cal, CalWORKs, or other DPSS/CDSS benefit denied, reduced, terminated, or changed
workflow_overrides.ca_statute: Welfare and Institutions Code §10950 (hearing rights); 22 CCR §22-071 (Medi-Cal hearings)

steps.description: Obtain written notice of action (NOA) from county DPSS. NOA must state specific reason and appeal deadline. Do not miss deadline — it is statutory and strict.
steps.deadline: Immediately — deadlines in NOA are strict

steps.description: Request State Hearing with CA Department of Social Services (CDSS) within 90 days of NOA date. Can request orally, in writing, or online. Request continued benefits simultaneously.
steps.documents_needed: Written or verbal request — reference NOA date
steps.agency_contact: CDSS: 800-952-5253 / benefitscal.com; or county DPSS office
steps.deadline: 90 days from NOA — benefits continue during appeal if timely requested

steps.description: Collect documents supporting eligibility: income records, medical documentation, housing records — anything refuting the denial reason.
steps.documents_needed: Documents specific to denial reason + provider documentation
steps.agency_contact: Personal records — request hearing date from CDSS
steps.deadline: Before hearing date

steps.description: Contact local legal aid before hearing. LA: LAFLA (800-399-4529). Bay Area: BALA (415-982-1300). IHSS denials: Disability Rights CA (800-776-5746). Free representation available.
steps.deadline: As soon as possible — legal aid calendars fill up quickly

steps.description: Hearing conducted by CDSS hearing officer. Present evidence. Bring advocate or attorney if possible. Decision binding on county.
steps.agency_contact: CDSS hearing — location or phone per hearing notice
steps.deadline: Attend all scheduled hearings or request continuance in advance

steps.description: If hearing decision adverse, petition for writ of mandate in Superior Court within 30 days. File complaint with CDSS Director or Governor's Office for systemic errors.
steps.deadline: 30 days from hearing decision for court appeal

workflow_overrides.situation: Health insurance claim denied in California — Medi-Cal managed care or private insurer
workflow_overrides.ca_statute: CA Insurance Code §10169; Health & Safety Code §1368 (IMR); Insurance Code §790.03 (bad faith)

steps.description: Collect denial letter, EOB, original claim, all correspondence. Note exact denial language and reason code.
steps.deadline: Immediately — appeal deadlines are strict

steps.description: File internal appeal with plan/insurer. ACA plans: 180 days from denial. Medi-Cal managed care: file grievance with plan within 60 days.
steps.documents_needed: Appeal letter, medical records, physician letter of medical necessity
steps.agency_contact: Insurer internal appeal per denial notice; Medi-Cal: plan grievance line
steps.deadline: ACA: 180 days. Medi-Cal managed care plan: 60 days.

steps.description: California-specific: request Independent Medical Review through CA Dept of Managed Health Care (DMHC). Free, binding, fast (within 30 days). Available for medical necessity denials. IMR is CA's strongest tool.
steps.documents_needed: Internal appeal denial + all medical records
steps.deadline: Within 6 months of internal denial

steps.description: File complaint with CA Dept of Managed Health Care (for HMOs/managed care) or CA Dept of Insurance (for PPO/indemnity plans). Documents pattern.
steps.deadline: Any time — does not affect IMR rights

steps.description: Medi-Cal managed care members: request State Hearing with CDSS (800-952-5253) if plan grievance fails. CDSS State Hearing independent of managed care plan.
steps.deadline: If plan grievance process fails — request within 90 days of denial

steps.description: Contact Disability Rights CA (800-776-5746) for disability-related denials. Bad faith insurance: private attorney. CA has strong bad faith laws (CC §790.03).
steps.deadline: If IMR denied or pattern of denials — consult legal aid or private attorney
